note: Claims the weather screens show (Prompt 09). Archive claims cite the W entries in data/sources_weather.json; numbers are read from the bundle products in data/weather/bundle (built by tools/weather/build_bundle.py). game_time and balance claims describe what the game changes and have no source.

claims.title: Where the weather comes from
claims.text: The weather in the game comes from real measurements made at Jezero crater on Mars by NASA's Perseverance rover and by a spacecraft orbiting Mars, between 2019 and 2022.
claims.note: Perseverance MEDA products for mission sols 289, 313, 317 and 579 (Dec 2021 to Oct 2022); dust optical depth from the LMD dust climatology built from Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter MCS retrievals, Mars years 35 and 36 (Mar 2019 to Dec 2022). Jezero crater is a real place, not the colony.

claims.title: Old measurements, played faster
claims.text: The weather screen shows old measurements from Jezero crater, played faster. It is not live weather and not a forecast for this colony.
claims.note: Archive observation dates are shown next to game time. Checking for archive updates never changes the weather of a running game.

claims.title: Measuring dust in the air
claims.text: Dust in the air is measured as optical depth. Over Jezero it was about 0.2 on clear days and rose to about 2 in a big dust storm in October 2022.
claims.note: Visible-equivalent column optical depth = 2.6 x the LMD 9.3 micron absorption value (factor from the LMD page), interpolated to Jezero. Mars year 36 range 0.20 to 2.03; the peak map is dated 5 Oct 2022 (Ls 316). Kriged maps, so this is worked out from orbital measurements, not measured at the rover.

claims.title: A dust storm reaches Jezero
claims.text: In early January 2022 a dust storm reached Jezero. In a few sols the dust optical depth there went from about 0.3 to about 0.8.
claims.note: LMD Mars year 36 maps at Jezero: 0.30 on 3 Jan 2022 (Ls 152.0), 0.81 on 8 Jan 2022 (Ls 155.2), back to 0.44 by 12 Jan. Episode jezero_my36_ls155 in the bundle.

claims.title: A wind sensor hurt by the weather
claims.text: Harsh weather damaged parts of Perseverance's wind sensor. The archive has no wind measurements after sol 315, in January 2022.
claims.note: MEDA release notes, section B.4. The derived wind collection lists sols 36 to 315. Most dust events in the game therefore have no measured wind.

claims.title: Air pressure at Jezero
claims.text: Air pressure at Jezero changes with the seasons. It averaged about 628 pascals on a sol in December 2021 and about 736 pascals on a sol in October 2022.
claims.note: Means of the measured 1 Hz derived pressure on mission sols 289 (Ls 140.6) and 579 (Ls 316.5). MEDA measures about half of each sol, so these are averages of the measured hours.

claims.title: Cold nights, cool afternoons
claims.text: On a clear sol in December 2021 the air at Jezero was about 196 K (-77 °C) before dawn and about 256 K (-17 °C) in the afternoon.
claims.note: 10-minute averages of the median of the three mast air temperature sensors, mission sol 289; coldest near 05 h and warmest near 15 h local mean solar time.

claims.title: Wind at Jezero
claims.text: On a clear sol in December 2021 the wind at Jezero blew at about 3 m/s on average, with gusts up to about 16 m/s.
claims.note: Mean and largest 1 Hz derived horizontal wind speed on mission sol 289 (measured hours only, rover still).

claims.title: Dust events copied from real ones
claims.text: Each dust event in the game copies the rise and fall of a real dust event seen over Jezero between 2020 and 2022.
claims.note: Nine episodes: periods when the optical depth over Jezero rose at least 0.35 above the usual sky for that season (data/weather/bundle/episodes.json).

claims.title: Storms come faster in the game
claims.text: In the game, dust events come sooner and closer together than they did at Jezero, and they last minutes instead of weeks. That is a game change, not how often storms happen on Mars.
claims.note: Gaps, durations and strength are scaled from the observed episodes by the game. They are a game transformation and say nothing about real storm frequency.

claims.title: Ready colonies see stronger storms
claims.text: How strong a dust event can get in the game depends on how ready the colony is: battery charge, a working panel cleaner and clean panels. That rule is game balance, not NASA data.
claims.note: The first event is always a small one, and only after the crew has learned to clean panels.

claims.title: Dust and solar power in the game
claims.text: The game turns dust optical depth into less solar power with a simple game rule. It is game balance, not a measurement of real panels.
claims.note: Atmosphere term exp(-0.6 x (tau - 0.5)) from docs/MODEL_P07.md; the episodes' solar_factor_at_peak uses the same rule.
